limitations: The finding is explicitly static and not executed.
Receiver aliasing, call ordering, conditional execution, and later resetting of settings can invalidate a source-level co-occurrence conclusion.
The Android API documents a permission policy for mixed content, not the presence of a particular HTTP URL or a successful malicious substitution.
CWE-319 requires sensitive or security-critical data in a sniffable cleartext channel; permissive mixed-content configuration alone does not prove that condition.
predicates: A receiver is an android.webkit.WebSettings instance obtained for, or otherwise associated with, an android.webkit.WebView.
An effective configuration write resolves to android.webkit.WebSettings.MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW.

For the complete reported configuration, JavaScript enablement, a true CookieManager.setAcceptThirdPartyCookies call for the same WebView, and a true setJavaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically write must be correlated by receiver and feasible control flow.
For the runtime mixed-content scenario, the configured WebView must load a secure-origin document that requests an insecure-origin resource.
detector_semantics.claim: The payment-screen construction path is statically reported as configuring a WebView with MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW. If that WebView renders an HTTPS page that requests HTTP content, the configuration can permit cleartext-network confidentiality and integrity risks. JavaScript, third-party cookies, and automatic window opening are co-occurring amplifiers, not prerequisites for mixed-content permission.

unknowns: Whether the supplied source-level settings configure one concrete WebView instance through all relevant control-flow paths.
Whether createPayCoreWebView is invoked in production and whether its result is used for an HTTPS cryptocurrency-payment flow.
Whether the payment page has HTTP subresources, and their origins, MIME types, and execution behavior.
Whether app manifest or Network Security Configuration settings permit cleartext HTTP for the applicable WebView and target SDK.
Whether any network attacker is positioned to observe or modify traffic in the relevant deployment.
Whether any cleartext request carries sensitive or security-critical data, as required to confirm CWE-319.
Whether third-party-cookie policy or automatic window opening has any realized impact in this flow.
Whether additional WebView controls, including URL allowlisting, WebViewClient interception, Safe Browsing, redirects, or page-side CSP, alter practical exposure.

documented_behavior: android.webkit.WebView.getSettings() returns the WebSettings object used to control that WebView.

android.webkit.WebSettings.setMixedContentMode(int), added in API level 21, configures behavior when a secure origin attempts to load a resource from an insecure origin. MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW is the least-secure mode and allows a secure origin to load content from an insecure origin.
android.webkit.WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled(true) enables JavaScript execution; its documented default is false.
android.webkit.CookieManager.setAcceptThirdPartyCookies(WebView, boolean), added in API level 21, sets a per-WebView policy for allowing third-party cookies to be set.
android.webkit.WebSettings.setJavaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically(true) allows JavaScript window.open calls without a user gesture; its documented default is false.

When multiple-window support is disabled, window.open and target=_blank requests are treated as top-level navigations in the same WebView. When enabled, application handling of WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow is required.
preconditions: The mixed-content setting is available beginning with Android API level 21.
A secure-origin document must attempt to load an insecure-origin resource for the documented mixed-content behavior to be implicated.
For JavaScript execution as an amplifier, JavaScript must be enabled and the relevant script must actually load and execute.
For third-party-cookie behavior, the true setting must apply to the particular WebView receiving third-party-cookie attempts.

For apps targeting API level 26 or higher, WebView honors the platform cleartext-traffic policy; an effective Network Security Configuration or manifest cleartext restriction can prevent the assumed HTTP fetch.
unknowns: The report does not identify the Android API level, targetSdkVersion, device WebView implementation, or effective Network Security Configuration.
The report does not establish whether a later code path changes mixedContentMode, disables JavaScript, changes cookie policy, destroys the WebView, or uses another WebView for payment content.
The report does not identify a top-level HTTPS URL, an HTTP subresource URL, the resource MIME type, or whether a request completed.
The report does not establish whether setSupportMultipleWindows or a WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow implementation exists.

events.condition: Observed: a source-level call or Kotlin property assignment names MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW. Predicate satisfied: the assigned value resolves to android.webkit.WebSettings.MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW, configures the WebSettings instance belonging to the WebView that later renders content, and is not superseded by a later effective mixed-content-mode write before the relevant load.
events.name: configure_mixed_content_always_allow

events.condition: Observed: JavaScript is enabled in source. Predicate satisfied: true reaches the WebSettings instance for the same rendered WebView at load time. This setting is not a prerequisite for permissive mixed-content loading itself, but is relevant to execution of a loaded script resource.
events.name: enable_javascript

events.condition: Observed: setAcceptThirdPartyCookies is called. Predicate satisfied: its second argument resolves to true and its WebView argument aliases the WebView whose settings permit mixed content. This per-WebView setting does not prove that any third-party cookie was set, sent, readable by an attacker, or relevant to the payment flow.
events.name: allow_third_party_cookies

events.condition: Observed: the automatic-window setting is assigned true. Predicate satisfied: true reaches the same WebView's WebSettings at the relevant time and JavaScript executes a window.open request without a user gesture. The setting alone does not prove creation of a separate window; that depends on multiple-window support and application WebChromeClient handling.
events.name: allow_javascript_automatic_window_opening

events.condition: Observed: source contains a possible WebView content-load call. Predicate satisfied only at runtime: the same configured WebView loads a secure-origin document and that document actually requests an insecure HTTP resource while the permissive setting remains effective. A loadUrl call alone establishes neither the top-level scheme nor the existence, type, or successful retrieval of an HTTP subresource.
events.name: load_secure_document_with_insecure_subresource

important_note: WebViewMixedContentSpec is a detector concern name, not a governed API type, CrySL rule, or Android/Java class. This context governs the actual Android APIs implicated by the finding. A static configuration match does not prove that createPayCoreWebView executed, that the configured WebView rendered a payment page, that an HTTPS page requested HTTP content, or that CWE-319 occurred at runtime.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That cash.p.terminal.modules.paycore.webview.PayCoreWebViewScreenKt.createPayCoreWebView executed in a released build or payment transaction.
That the configured WebView loaded an HTTPS payment page rather than local, HTTP, test, or no content.
That an HTTPS page requested an HTTP subresource or that WebView successfully fetched it.
That an HTTP subresource was JavaScript, that it executed, or that it was security-sensitive.
That a network attacker intercepted, modified, or replaced an HTTP response.
That secrets, credentials, wallet material, payment data, cookies, or other security-critical data traversed cleartext; such evidence is necessary for CWE-319.
That enabled third-party-cookie acceptance resulted in a third-party cookie being set, sent, or usable in the affected flow.
That gestureless window opening created a new WebView or window; honoring a separate window depends on multiple-window support and application WebChromeClient handling.
That JavaScript acquired native application privileges; this requires separate evidence such as an exposed JavaScript interface or another privileged bridge.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: A runtime CWE-319 finding requires evidence that sensitive or security-critical information was transmitted through a cleartext channel that an unauthorized actor could sniff. For the reported script-replacement scenario, runtime evidence must additionally show an HTTP subresource request, that the request was permitted and received, and an attacker-capable network path or an observed modified response. Cleartext traffic can be read and manipulated by network observers.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The observed configuration is a potential mixed-content weakness: an HTTPS-origin page rendered by the affected WebView may be allowed to request HTTP content, which lacks transport confidentiality and integrity protections.

compatibility: Identify the device API level and targetSdkVersion because setMixedContentMode was added in API level 21 and historical default behavior varies by target SDK.
Identify the effective manifest and Network Security Configuration cleartext policy because WebView honors the cleartext-traffic flag for apps targeting API level 26 and higher.
Identify the installed WebView provider and version when behavioral reproduction is required.
Identify whether multiple-window support and WebChromeClient.onCreateWindow handling are present before characterizing automatic window opening as creation of a separate window.
runtime: Record the effective mixed-content mode on the WebView at navigation time.
Record a secure HTTPS top-level document rendered in that WebView and an attempted HTTP subresource request.
Determine whether the HTTP request was actually allowed, completed, blocked by policy, redirected, or intercepted.
If asserting script impact, identify the fetched resource as executable script and show that it executed in the page context.
If asserting CWE-319, identify security-critical or sensitive data carried over the cleartext channel, or narrowly state an integrity-only mixed-content result rather than CWE-319.
source_level: Resolve the receiver of getSettings()/WebSettings writes to the same android.webkit.WebView instance used by the payment flow.
Resolve the mixed-content argument to WebSettings.MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW rather than an unknown integer or guarded alternative.
Establish feasible ordering: the permissive setting is effective before the relevant navigation and is not later overwritten.
For auxiliary settings, establish that JavaScript, third-party cookies, and automatic window opening are enabled on the same WebView rather than merely elsewhere in the process.

name: WebViewMixedContentSpec
semantic_scope: The detector finding is a static candidate centered on permissive android.webkit.WebSettings mixed-content configuration in createPayCoreWebView, with JavaScript enabled, third-party cookies allowed, and gestureless JavaScript window opening reported as co-occurring settings. Its direct observation is configuration that can permit insecure-origin content to be loaded from a secure-origin document. It does not, from the supplied finding alone, observe network traffic, response contents, page origin, subresource type, execution, attacker control, or sensitive-data transmission.
known_false_positive_shapes: The configuration occurs in dead, test-only, preview-only, or otherwise unreachable code.
The configured WebView is never navigated to content, is destroyed before navigation, or is not the WebView used for payment content.
A later feasible write changes the effective mixed-content mode to MIXED_CONTENT_NEVER_ALLOW before the relevant page load.

The WebView renders only HTTP, local, data:, or other non-secure-origin content; this may present other concerns but does not satisfy the documented secure-origin-to-insecure-origin mixed-content condition.
All rendered HTTPS content has no HTTP subresources.
The platform cleartext policy blocks HTTP traffic in the WebView, including for an app targeting API level 26 or higher where WebView honors that policy.
JavaScript is enabled but no mixed HTTP script loads or executes.
Third-party cookies are permitted but no third-party cookie is requested, accepted, or relevant to the page session.
Automatic window opening is enabled but no window.open call occurs, or requests are not honored as separate windows by the application's multiple-window/WebChromeClient handling.
protocol: WebView.getSettings() -> WebSettings.setMixedContentMode(MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW) -> WebView loads an HTTPS-origin document -> that document requests an HTTP subresource -> WebView permits the insecure subresource; JavaScript, third-party-cookie, and automatic-window settings are separate amplifiers when enabled on the same WebView.

detector_examples.message: Static candidate (not executed): the payment WebView of a cryptocurrency wallet sets mixedContentMode = MIXED_CONTENT_ALWAYS_ALLOW with JavaScript, third-party cookies and automatic window opening enabled, so plain-HTTP subresources -- including scripts -- load inside HTTPS payment pages and can be replaced by a network attacker (CWE-319).
